newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -Gilts capped by downtrend at 109-17.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -Gilts capped by downtrend at 109-17.

text.p: June gilt futures traded on LIFFE will be unable to break above trendline resistance drawn from a high in mid-April, technical analysts said on Monday.
Analysts said last week's price action had been largely bearish, and the trendline from the April 17 high of 110-10 was likely to keep rises in check during the early part of the week.
"It's not oversold, and if it wants to go down there is plenty of scope," said Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
June gilt futures were up 2/32 at 108-26 by 0705 GMT, after opening flat.
Cossor said the market was also facing resistance from old supports at 109-07/08 before it could take on 109-17.
Susan Rigg, technical analyst at Chart Analysis in London told Reuters Financial Television the market had the chance to push ahead once the election on Thursday was out of the way.
"Instead of being turned back at the 50 percent level as in Bunds and notionnel we got turned back at the 38 percent level," she said.
A 50 percent Fibonacci retracement of the downmove from 113-19 on February 18 to a low of 108-05 on April 1 is 110-28, while a 38.2 percent retracement comes out at 110-06.
Cossor said downside moves were likely to be "a grind rather than a rout", as volume on Friday when the market set a low of 108-21, was lower than during the previous session.
He cited support at 108-14, the April 11 low, and then at 108-05, the nadir for the month made on April 1.
At the short end, June short sterling futures were down one basis point at 93.33 by 0718 GMT.
